Performers
Felix Galimir (violin I), Adrienne Galimir (spelled “Adrielle” in the item description) (violin II), Renée Galimir (viola), Marguerite Galimir (cello) Documented

The advertisement names the “Galimir String Quartet of Vienna”. The item description lists the four players. The second violinist’s name is “Adrielle” there and Adrienne in the Boston Symphony Orchestra note, which says the quartet consisted of a brother and three sisters.

[1] [2] [3]
Work version
Berg’s Lyric Suite for string quartet (the 1926 quartet version); the edition used by the performers is not stated. Documented

The Internet Archive description gives the title and “for string quartet (1926)”; the advertisement of 1937 gives “Suite Lyrique. For String Quartet”. The movement is the third of six; the file runs 3:42 and carries the whole movement.

[1] [2]
Recorded
c. 1935–⁠36 Documented

Stated in the item description (“Recorded c. 1935-36”). Wikipedia’s list of recordings gives “ca. 1935”; no session ledger was seen.

[1] [4]
Place
Paris Documented

Stated in the item description, which says the recording was made “for French Polydor”. The label of the American disc 95007 reads “Recorded in France”.

[1] [5]
Label
Polydor (France); Decca (Great Britain); Brunswick-⁠Polydor (United States) Documented

The item description lists the three issues and adds a reissue by Vox in July 1948. The March 1937 advertisement shows the American issue by Brunswick-⁠Polydor.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
Brunswick-⁠Polydor set BP No. 2 (records 95006–⁠95009; slide-automatic set BP-2A, 95010–⁠95013); earlier issues Polydor 516.659–⁠516.662 and Decca CA-8244–⁠8247 as given in the item description Documented

The set number BP No. 2 is confirmed by the March 1937 advertisement and by the label photograph of disc 95007; the Polydor and Decca numbers and the British issue date (December 1936) are from the item description only. Wikipedia’s list of recordings gives the first issue as Polydor 595.135–⁠595.138; the two sets of numbers were not reconciled.

[1] [2] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
Brunswick-⁠Polydor 95007, “In 8 Parts”, Part III, with the third movement named on the label; matrix and take numbers are not given Documented

Read from the label photograph in the Internet Archive item (“Part III … Set No. BP-2 … Third Movement: Allegro misterioso”). The item description and the label give no matrix or take numbers. The files are labelled (i) to (vi), one for each movement.

[5]
Transfer
Internet Archive collection shellackophile-recordings; no individual transfer credit Documented

The item names a collection but no transfer engineer.

[1]
Transfer date
Not stated; the item was made public on 13 March 2022 Unknown

The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

[1]
Processing
Each movement is one file, uploaded as FLAC with an MP3 derivative; equalisation and noise reduction are not described. Unknown

The published MP3 is the Internet Archive derivative.

[1]
Composition rights
Berg died in 1935, so the work has been in the public domain in the EU and other life-plus-70 countries since 2006. Its United States status is not assessed here. Documented

Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording.

[3]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; the American issue was advertised by March 1937. Documented

The item description gives earlier French and British issues, which were not checked in a second source. The United States status of a recording made in France in the 1930s is not established.

[2]

Alban Berg, Lyric Suite, III. Galimir String Quartet of Vienna. Recorded c. 1935–⁠36; issued as Brunswick-⁠Polydor set BP No. 2, advertised in March 1937. Internet Archive item bp-2-berg-suite-lyrique-iv (collection shellackophile-recordings). Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established. Rights statement
